name: Brandenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Charming scattered village in the Brandenberger Tal valley, featuring the Wildbachklamm gorge and untouched nature nestled between the Alps.
beschreibung:
Overview

Brandenberg is an expansive mountain municipality in Tyrol's Kufstein district, situated at an elevation of approximately 920 meters in a densely forested high valley north of the Lower Inn Valley. Home to around 1,540 residents, the municipality spans more than 130 square kilometers between the rugged limestone faces of the Rofan Mountains and the Brandenberg Alps. Defined by deep river gorges, lush mixed alpine woodlands, and the roaring Brandenberger Ache torrent, the area serves as an oasis of natural tranquility away from commercial tourism. Dispersed hamlets including Brandenberg-Dorf, Pinegg, and Aschau dot the plateau, offering pristine alpine experiences for hikers, nature lovers, and whitewater kayakers.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1140. Its name originates from medieval slash-and-burn clearing practices, literally translating to burning mountain. For over five hundred years between 1412 and 1966, the valley served as the regional epicenter of timber log driving (Holztrift): massive volumes of harvested mountain timber were flushed down the raging Brandenberger Ache to fuel smelting works in Brixlegg and the Hall in Tirol salt mine. The daring wooden walkways once used by log-driving lumberjacks were later converted into today's visitor footpaths. The historic Kaiserhaus lodge in Pinegg hosted royal hunting parties; when Emperor Franz Joseph I and Empress Sisi visited to witness the timber drive, the Kaiserklamm gorge received its imperial moniker. The parish church dedicated to Saint George in Brandenberg-Dorf was erected between 1678 and 1680, standing as one of the earliest purely Baroque sacred buildings in the Tyrolean Unterland.

How to Get There

By car, Brandenberg is reached via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Kramsach/Brixlegg and following provincial road L4 up the mountain in about fifteen minutes. The road winds from Kramsach to Brandenberg-Dorf and continues through Pinegg to the Alpengasthof Kaiserhaus. Rail passengers travel to Brixlegg or Rattenberg-Kramsach railway station, connecting with hourly VVT regional bus line 610 into the valley, complemented by summer hiking shuttles extending to the Kaiserklamm.

Tips

Among the most dramatic natural spectacles in Tyrol are the Kaiserklamm and Tiefenbachklamm gorges, featuring secure rock-cut walkways, suspended bridges, and tunnels along emerald waters. A celebrated culinary trademark is the Brandenberger Prügeltorte, an authentic festive spit cake baked layer by layer over open beechwood fires on rotating wooden rollers, recognized as intangible cultural heritage; demonstrations take place at the historic Kaiserhaus inn. Mountain bikers and long-distance hikers can venture to the Erzherzog-Johann-Klause splash dam near the Bavarian border. The Brandenberger Ache river also attracts whitewater kayakers from across Europe.
